paper.title: Mersenne Twister: a 623-dimensionally equidistributed uniform pseudo-random number generator
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Modeling and Computer Simulation 8(1)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the paper's recurrence (n=624, m=397, r=31, twist constant 9908b0df) and tempering; the 2002 seeding routines (init_genrand, init_by_array) were re-implemented from the authors' reference source, which is where their multipliers are defined; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: after init_by_array({0x123, 0x234, 0x345, 0x456}) the first 1000 outputs of the 32-bit generator equal the 1000 values the authors published
a default-seeded (5489) mt19937 produces 4123659995 as its 10000th output, the value the C++ standard requires

expected_values_source.what: the 1000 genrand_int32() outputs in the authors' mt19937ar.out; the 10000th-output value from the C++ standard draft ([rand.predef], mt19937)
expected_values_source.note: the values are data, copied as numbers; the authors' code was read only to confirm the seeding constants and was not copied. The 10000th-output value is from the C++ standard, not from the 1998 paper.

negative_control: built with -DMT_M=396 (middle offset 396 instead of 397), 0 of 1000 published outputs match, the 10000th-output check fails and the program exits 1 (checked on ounce-core Tier-3 and natively)
not_checked: the paper's equidistribution (623-dimensional) and period 2^19937-1 claims
the real-valued outputs (genrand_real*), which the authors' .out file also lists
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
the original 1998 seeding routine (the published outputs use the 2002 init_by_array)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 1000 published MT19937 outputs and the standard's 10000th value. It does not show the statistical claims hold.
